findings.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial-cache key omits `checkReq.Folder`, so checks differing only in `Folder` map to the same denial key; a legitimately-denied check for folder A poisons subsequent checks for folder B until the TTL expires

[Medium/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial-cache key uses raw `checkReq.UserUID` without including `IdentityType`, unlike `permCache` keys which use resolved internal UID; a user and service account with the same UID string share a denial-cache entry, so a denial for one identity type incorrectly denies the other

[Medium/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — `permDenialCache` entries are never invalidated when permissions/role assignments change; existing cache-invalidation paths are not updated for the new keyspace, so a newly granted permission continues to be denied for up to `shortCacheTTL`

[Medium/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial-cache keys are built from client-controlled, unbounded-length strings (`Name`, `ParentFolder`) with no cardinality limit, allowing any authenticated caller to grow the local cache indefinitely (memory-exhaustion vector)

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:128 — Any error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (including real errors from `GetUserIdentifiers`, not just `cache.ErrNotFound`) is silently swallowed and treated as a cache miss, masking genuine lookup failures and causing repeated identifier lookups in `getIdentityPermissions`

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:128 — `permissionCacheUsage` is incremented with `"false"` when cached evaluation yields `allowed == false` even though the cache was hit, conflating cache miss with cached denial and making the cache-hit-rate metric inaccurate

[Low/test_gap] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:893 — `TestService_CacheCheck` lacks cases for: (a) permission-grant invalidation vs. stale denial entries, (b) user vs. service-account key collision, (c) verifying `List` ignores the denial cache, and (d) that the fallback path repopulates `permCache` with fresh permissions

[Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates fields with `_` without escaping; client- or externally-supplied `name`/`parent`/`userUID` values containing `_` can cause ambiguity collisions between distinct (user, action, name, parent) tuples

[Low/doc_defect] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:53 — The struct comment still reads "Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles" but the struct now also holds `permDenialCache`; the comment was not updated

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial-cache key omits `checkReq.Folder`, so checks differing only in `Folder` map to the same denial key; a legitimately-denied check for folder A poisons subsequent checks for folder B until the TTL expires

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the denial key is constructed as `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, checkReq.Action, checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)`, and `userPermDenialCacheKey` explicitly includes the final `parent` argument in the key string (`... + "_" + parent`). So the denial-cache key *does* incorporate the folder/parent-folder dimension via `checkReq.ParentFolder`; it is not omitted in the diff. The added test `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry` also uses `userPermDenialCacheKey(..., "fold1")` alongside a request with `Folder: "fold1"`, consistent with the folder value being part of the key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial-cache key uses raw `checkReq.UserUID` without including `IdentityType`, unlike `permCache` keys which use resolved internal UID; a user and service account with the same UID string share a denial-cache entry, so a denial for one identity type incorrectly denies the other

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the denial-cache key is built as `userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, checkReq.UserUID, action, name, parentFolder)` (service.go around the added code). That key does not include `IdentityType` and uses the raw `checkReq.UserUID`, while cached permission lookups for users/service accounts resolve identifiers via `GetUserIdentifiers` and then key on `userIdentifiers.UID` (`getCachedIdentityPermissions`). As a result, two different identity types that present the same `UserUID` string in the request would share the same denial entry and could incorrectly deny each other.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — `permDenialCache` entries are never invalidated when permissions/role assignments change; existing cache-invalidation paths are not updated for the new keyspace, so a newly granted permission continues to be denied for up to `shortCacheTTL`

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `permDenialCache` in `Service.Check`: it short-circuits to `Allowed: false` if a denial key exists (`permDenialCache.Get(...)`), and it sets that key whenever a DB-backed check returns `!allowed` (`permDenialCache.Set(...)`). There is no code in the diff that ever removes or bypasses an existing denial entry when permissions change, so a subsequently granted permission would still be denied until the `shortCacheTTL` expires. This behavior is directly verifiable from the new early-return denial path and the absence of any invalidation/override logic in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial-cache keys are built from client-controlled, unbounded-length strings (`Name`, `ParentFolder`) with no cardinality limit, allowing any authenticated caller to grow the local cache indefinitely (memory-exhaustion vector)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new denial cache in `Service.Check` keyed by `userPermDenialCacheKey(...)`, which concatenates request-derived fields `checkReq.Name` and `checkReq.ParentFolder` into the cache key (`namespace + ... + "_" + name + "_" + parent`). These values come from the client request and are not bounded or normalized in the shown code, and the underlying local cache has no cardinality/size limit visible in this diff. This allows an authenticated caller to generate many unique denial keys (or very long keys) and grow the in-memory cache until eviction by TTL, creating a memory-exhaustion vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:128 — Any error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (including real errors from `GetUserIdentifiers`, not just `cache.ErrNotFound`) is silently swallowed and treated as a cache miss, masking genuine lookup failures and causing repeated identifier lookups in `getIdentityPermissions`

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are ignored (only the err==nil path is used); on any error it falls through to getIdentityPermissions without logging the cache-path failure. In getCachedIdentityPermissions, the user/serviceaccount path calls GetUserIdentifiers and can return a real error (not just cache.ErrNotFound), so this can indeed cause an extra identifier lookup when getIdentityPermissions runs and can also hide intermittent identifier lookup failures if the subsequent DB path succeeds. However, it does not necessarily break correctness because getIdentityPermissions will still error and be logged if the underlying failure persists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:128 — `permissionCacheUsage` is incremented with `"false"` when cached evaluation yields `allowed == false` even though the cache was hit, conflating cache miss with cached denial and making the cache-hit-rate metric inaccurate

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, a cache lookup is performed via `getCachedIdentityPermissions`; however `permissionCacheUsage` is only incremented with `"true"` when the cached evaluation returns `allowed == true` (early return). If cached permissions are found but `allowed == false`, the code falls through and later increments `permissionCacheUsage` with `"false"` (`s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", checkReq.Action).Inc()`), which mixes “cache miss” with “cache hit but not sufficient/denied/outdated”, making the metric ambiguous/inaccurate for hit-rate purposes. This is a metrics/observability semantics issue, not a functional correctness defect.
